title: Designing a Bio-responsive Robot from DNA Origami
protocol: Download and install caDNAno 2.0 and Autodesk Maya 2012.
Create an academic account at http://students.autodesk.com/.
After receiving the account setup e-mail, click the activation link and fill in your preferences as desired.
Download the free version of Maya 2012 from the download center.
Install Maya 2012 on your computer.
Run Maya once before installing caDNAno 2.0.
Download and install the latest version of caDNAno 2.0 from http://cadnano.org/.
Run Maya 2012.
A caDNAno icon should appear at the top right corner of the graphical user interface.
Click the icon to go into caDNAno.
Outline the desired DNA nanostructure shape on the left lattice view panel in caDNAno.
Zoom into the lattice using mouse scroll up for closer inspection.
Select double DNA helices by left-clicking their center circles to build the initial shape outline.
Continue selecting helices until the entire shape is outlined.
Alternatively, draw the shape continuously by pressing and dragging with the left mouse button.
Use Edit menu or keyboard shortcut (CTRL+Z on PC/CMD+Z on Mac) to undo any action.
Observe the selected helices appearing yellow in the lattice view panel.
View a side section of the shape in the bottom editing panel, which shows single base-level actions.
Extend the scaffold path by dragging the selected edges as a group to the left side of the grid.
Repeat this process for the right edges until the path is properly extended.
Locate the scaffold path parts that are isolated from the rest, and connect them.
Zoom in on the strands to be connected, and using the "Select" tool click on any point on one of the strands.
Upon clicking any point along a blue scaffold fragment, bridge icons appear between helices.
Left click the bridge icon of choice to create crossovers.
Repeat this process until the scaffold traverses all helices and creates a closed loop that spans the entire shape.
Leave no regions isolated from the rest of the shape.
Inject 270 μl of resulting solution.
Erase the existing crossover between helices 29-30.
Create a new crossover between helices 29-30 near the left edge of the grid.
Create a new crossover between helices 61 and 0 near the left edge of the grid.
Define payload attachment sites as staple strands extending from helices 3, 27, 34, and 58.
Plot an additional helix to guide directional branching of staples for precise extension.
Remove the guide helix after extending the desired loading site staple.
Click the helix immediately adjacent to the designated helices that faces the internal side in the top panel.
Add and edit staples using the "AutoStaple" function.
Click "AutoBreak".
Set default parameters for staple breaking.
Erase all staple crossovers between helices 29-30 and 61-0.
Ensure scaffold crossovers from sections 3.2 and 3.3 remain intact.
Select the first staple crossover between helices 29 and 30.
Click each knee point or bridge of the selected crossover to turn red.
Delete the bridges by hitting DELETE.
Seam the two staples on helix 29 by pressing SHIFT and clicking the nick between them.
Seam the three staples on strand 30 to a single staple.
Manually extend or shorten staples as desired without circularizing any staple.
Locate staples drawn by a thick line, indicating they require further editing.
Correct short staples by erasing or extending if possible.
Second-click the loading site helices in the top panel.
Extend resulting scaffold strand fragments in the bottom panel by clicking and dragging an edge.
Manually add staples to scaffold fragments by placing the orange vertical bar at desired positions along the scaffold, holding SHIFT and clicking guide helices on the left panel.
Extend staple precursors to full length by clicking and dragging.
Locate red bridge icons denoting allowed crossover positions between guide strands and chassis.
Choose the most convenient location to introduce a crossover and click the bridge icon.
In the guide helix (helix 62), delete the staple part that is not part of the loading site.
Shorten the participating part in the guide helix to the desired length, typically an 18-mer tail.
Ensure the staple remains drawn by a thin line; if necessary, edit it until it is.
Edit the changed staples as necessary in the chassis.
Erase the guide (helix 62) leaving only the staple extension.
Repeat steps for all loading sites.
Click the edge of one potential gate strand to extend it outside of the shape.
Make sure only "Stap"(les) are selectable in the "Selectable" toolbar on the top right side of the interface.
Extend both staples to form the gate strands.
Edit the staples if this extension requires it.
Choose Scaffold Sequence.
Click the "Seq" tool.
Place cursor anywhere on the scaffold strand and click.
Simulate results in CANDO after the job is saved as a .json file.
Upload the .json file to CANDO for analysis.
Click "Submit a caDNAno file for analysis" and fill all necessary information.
Analysis in CANDO usually takes up to 15-20 minutes.
At the end, an email message notifies that the analysis is complete.
Download the simulation results from the provided link.
